references.text: The same list of peoples (Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites) and the description of the land flowing with milk and honey
The same list of nations that lived in the promised land
God's oath to the fathers to give them the land
Reiteration of the promise of the land flowing with milk and honey, and the list of nations
The same list of nations that the Lord will drive out
God's covenant with Abraham to give his descendants the land, with a list of nations
Joseph's reference to the oath God swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob concerning the land
A similar promise that the Lord will bring the people into the land with the same nations mentioned
The description of the promised land flowing with milk and honey
The land flowing with milk and honey, which God swore to the fathers
The fulfillment of the promise of the land flowing with milk and honey
The spies' confirmation that the land truly flows with milk and honey
Caleb and Joshua's testimony about the land flowing with milk and honey
A direct parallel in the same chapter describing the introduction to the gift of the land and its consequences.
Theological connection between God's oath concerning the land and the requirement of obedience to retain it.
Two different response actions (service and lawgiving) linked to the same entry into the promised land.
Historical confirmation that the promise of land given in Exodus was indeed fulfilled.
Prophetic reminder of God's faithfulness to the same oath-promise mentioned in Exodus.
Theological contrast: The entry leading to service (13:5) versus the entry leading to idolatry (31:20).
